name: Checkpointing for Reverse-Mode Memory Optimization
definition: An optimization to reduce the memory complexity of reverse-mode automatic differentiation by storing only a subset of intermediate variables (checkpoints) and recomputing the loop segments between them during the reverse pass.
summary: Checkpointing reduces reverse-mode memory to logarithmic levels by storing sparse states and recomputing segments, serving as a general-purpose alternative to problem-specific differentiation methods.
